questions.q: What does COUNT return when used on a text column?
options: 0 — COUNT only counts rows with a non-blank numeric value
The number of distinct text values
The number of non-blank rows, regardless of type
An error
questions.explain: COUNT only counts numeric values. Use COUNTA to count non-blank values of any type, including text.

questions.q: What's the difference between COUNTA and COUNTROWS?
options: COUNTA counts non-blank values in a specific column; COUNTROWS counts table rows regardless of column content
They are exactly the same function with two names
COUNTROWS only works on numeric columns
COUNTA counts table rows; COUNTROWS counts non-blank values in a column
questions.explain: COUNTA looks at one column's non-blank values, while COUNTROWS simply counts how many rows exist in a table (or filtered subset), ignoring column content.

options: The number of distinct (unique) values in a column
The total of all numeric values in a column
The number of rows in a table
The largest value in a column
questions.explain: DISTINCTCOUNT counts how many unique values appear in a column — for example, how many unique order numbers exist, not how many order rows exist.

questions.q: Why can a DISTINCTCOUNT grand total be smaller than the sum of its category-level values?
options: Because a value counted as distinct within multiple categories is still only counted once in the overall total
Because DISTINCTCOUNT rounds down at the total level
Because DISTINCTCOUNT ignores blank values in the total but not in categories
This never happens — DISTINCTCOUNT totals always equal the sum of their parts
questions.explain: An order appearing in two categories is counted once per category, but only once overall — so the grand total reflects distinct values across the whole dataset, not a sum of category counts.

questions.q: If you need a total that always adds up cleanly across categories, which function should you use instead of DISTINCTCOUNT?
options: COUNT or COUNTROWS
AVERAGE
MIN
There is no alternative — DISTINCTCOUNT totals can never add up
questions.explain: COUNT and COUNTROWS count rows, not unique values, so their totals are simple sums of their category-level numbers — though the resulting count will differ from a distinct count.
